Route 1: Impregnation method for 10Co3O4@CeO2

1. Prepare the CeO2 support by weighing 0.45 g of pre-synthesized CeO2 powder (spherical morphology, ~500 nm particle size). This CeO2 will serve as the seed/support for cobalt oxide deposition.

2. Dissolve Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.06 g) in deionized water (50.0 mL) to form a clear pink solution. Stir at room temperature until complete dissolution.

3. Add the CeO2 powder to the cobalt nitrate solution and stir vigorously to ensure uniform dispersion. Adjust the pH to approximately 7.0 using dilute ammonia solution if necessary.

4. Heat the suspension to 90°C under continuous stirring to evaporate the solvent gradually. Maintain this temperature until the mixture becomes a thick slurry.

5. Transfer the dried material to a crucible and calcine in air at 400–500°C for 2–4 hours to decompose the cobalt nitrate and form Co3O4 crystallites on the CeO2 surface.

6. Allow the product to cool to room temperature, then collect and gently grind the powder.

Final product: 10Co3O4@CeO2 composite material consisting of Co3O4 nanoparticles supported on spherical CeO2 particles. The product exhibits a cubic crystal system for both phases, spherical morphology with approximate particle size of 500 nm × 500 nm × 500 nm. Phase identification matches PDF references 42-1467 (CeO2, cubic fluorite) and 34-0394 (Co3O4, cubic spinel).
